info.title: State trial-court caseloads by court level, county and case type: Texas district, constitutional county and statutory county courts, fiscal years 2023–24 and 2024–25: data API
info.summary: Static, read-only JSON and CSV files. No key, no sign-up. CORS open.
info.description:
State trial-court caseloads by court level, county and case type: Texas district, constitutional county and statutory county courts, fiscal years 2023–24 and 2024–25: How many cases are added to Texas trial-court dockets, by county, court level and case group, from the Office of Court Administration's annual statistical reports: district courts (civil, family, juvenile, criminal), constitutional county courts (civil, criminal, juvenile) and statutory county courts (civil, family, juvenile, felony, misdemeanor), for Texas fiscal years 2024 and 2025 (September 1 to August 31). The state rows also give district-court filings by case type: motor-vehicle injury, medical malpractice, other injury or damage, product liability, contract, real property, family and criminal types. Each record gives the cases added, the year before, the cases disposed and the cases pending at year end, and a rate per 100,000 residents for county rows. In every table the counties add up exactly to the report's own statewide row, and the district-court rows reconcile to the separate Activity Detail workbook. Counts only: no lawyer or firm is listed or ranked. The schema carries a state code so other states' machine-readable caseloads can be added under the same keys; case types are compared only within a state.

Probative is a marketing firm, not a law firm; not legal advice. Every JSON response starts with a "meta" object holding the credit line, citation, DOI and license (CC BY 4.0).
